notes.scout: At 30, Rodrigo was not a player ascending toward something, he was a player holding a line, carrying attacking intent for a side that spent the year fighting the drop with Bielsa's system suddenly exposed at Premier League pace. A VV score of 70 tells you what the eye already suspected: the output was real, but the context around it was too chaotic, too depleted, too desperate to elevate these numbers into something the radar could celebrate. What it costs to deny is this: in a Leeds shirt that season, six goals from the ten was not a contribution, it was load-bearing.
notes.glance: Six goals from a central attacking midfielder at Leeds United, in a season that asked everything of everyone and gave very little back, is not a footnote, it is a survival story.

The Role Rarity dimension of the VV Index exists for seasons precisely like this one. The same output from a number ten would be noted. From a full-back, it bends the position's definition.
He did not reinvent the role. He simply played it so far beyond its traditional ceiling that the ceiling is no longer a useful reference point.
notes.scout: There is a case, carefully constructed across four seasons now, that Alexander-Arnold has permanently altered what we expect a full-back to deliver creatively. The 21/22 season does not open that case. It closes it. An RT of 83, the Provider tag earned not gifted, and the Iron Man designation confirming he carried this workload across the full campaign, not in bursts. To look at twelve assists from a defensive position in the Premier League and call it anything other than structurally rare would be to misread what football actually asks of that role.
notes.glance: Twelve assists from right-back, in the most demanding league on earth, at twenty-three, wearing the number sixty-six for a club that demanded everything and received it.

Four goals across a Premier League campaign is not a statistic, it is a wound. At an age when Thierry Henry was sharpening, when Ronaldo was accelerating, Rashford was managing the gap between what his body allowed and what his talent demanded.

The VV score of 71 carries no tags, and that absence is its own evidence. notes.scout: At 24, Rashford should have been peaking, the body and the mind converging on something sustained and serious. Instead, a shoulder injury carried from the summer and a club in structural freefall produced a season that reads less like a chapter and more like a dropped sentence. Scouts do not discount the ability, they cannot, but they note the distance between what this player is and what this season was.
notes.glance: Four goals, two assists, and the quiet devastation of a talent that had promised the world and, this season, could not find the door.

notes: Harry Kane at 28 for Tottenham in 2021/22 was the picture of a man who had accepted his circumstances without surrendering to them. He led, he created, he finished, and he did it in a league that punishes any weakness in the players around you.

Twenty-six direct goal contributions from a striker whose club finished in the top four only on the final day tells you something about the weight he carried. The assists, nine of them, confirm what every defender already knew: Kane reads the game at a different altitude to most, and his passing range has always been the secret the highlights never quite capture.

The Iron Man tag is not decoration here. It is the whole story. Seventeen goals and nine assists across a Premier League season, rating 89 on the VV Index, in a Spurs side cycling through tactical identities under Nuno and then Conte. Availability is a form of courage when the team around you is uncertain.
He stayed. He produced. And somewhere in that gap between what he gave and what he received, the most complete centre-forward in England kept building a case that deserved a bigger courtroom.
notes.scout: At 28, Kane was entering the years when a striker's body and mind converge into something complete, the moment a career should crystallise around silverware and stages worthy of the talent. Instead, he was Iron Man in a club still building its philosophy around his presence, the most reliable thing in a system that could not decide what it wanted to be. You cannot look at this season and deny the quality; you can only ask what it might have looked like somewhere else.
notes.glance: Seventeen goals, nine assists, and the quiet devastation of a man who gave Tottenham everything while Tottenham gave him nothing back.

notes: Tottenham in 2021/22 were a club searching for an identity, changing managers mid-season, losing their figurehead to the treatment room for long stretches. Son did not wait for the chaos to resolve. He stepped into the vacancy and filled it with goals.

There is a particular kind of pressure that comes from being the one a crowd turns to when the obvious answer is unavailable. Son carried it without theatre, week after week, in a league that punishes any hesitation. Twenty-three goals in the Premier League. Seven assists alongside them.

The tags tell the fuller story: Goal Machine and Clinical for the finishing that earned him the Golden Boot, Playmaker for the seven assists that show he was never merely a finisher, Iron Man for the availability across a season when Tottenham could afford to lose no one else. These were not isolated moments of quality. They were sustained, deliberate, repeated.
At 29, most forwards have already shown you everything they are. Son chose this season to show you something new.
notes.scout: At 29, with Harry Kane absent through injury and the weight of a club's attacking ambition falling entirely on his shoulders, Son did not buckle under the responsibility, he defined himself through it. A VV rating of 91 at this age, in this league, carrying this load, is not a number you explain away. It is a career-shaping season, and any serious assessment of what Son is as a footballer has to begin here.
notes.glance: Twenty-three goals, no Kane for months, and Son Heung-Min became the thing Tottenham had always needed him to be, not the support act, but the show itself.

notes: Kevin De Bruyne at thirty played like a man who had finally run out of patience with understatement. Manchester City built their entire attacking architecture around his movement, his weight of pass, his reading of spaces that existed for perhaps a half-second before closing forever.

The age is the detail that stops you. Thirty is when most creative midfielders begin their negotiation with decline, the pace gone, the influence diluted, the system asked to carry them rather than be carried by them. De Bruyne refused that negotiation entirely.

The tags on this season earn their place one by one: Goal Machine because fifteen goals from midfield in the Premier League demands that word, Clinical because he wasted nothing, Provider and Playmaker because the eight assists tell only part of the creative story, and Maestro because there is no other word for someone who conducts a Pep Guardiola side and makes it feel like his own. The VV score of 88 reflects a player operating at the outer edge of what this position, in this league, can produce.
Thirty years old, and still the first name on the teamsheet, still the one Guardiola built around. Some players age. De Bruyne just kept going.
notes.scout: This was the season De Bruyne stopped being described and started being accepted, the argument about whether he was the best midfielder in England finally exhausted by the weight of evidence he kept producing. Fifteen goals from a central attacking midfield role in the Premier League is not a midfielder's return, it is a forward's, and he achieved it while also anchoring City's entire creative structure. You cannot coach what he did this year. You can only hope your system survives it.
notes.glance: At thirty, Kevin De Bruyne did not slow down, he simply decided what mattered, and the Premier League had no answer.

notes: Manchester United in 2021/22 were a club searching for an identity they had lost a decade before. The return of Ronaldo was sold as a solution. What it became was a mirror, reflecting every structural problem the club had refused to fix, while one man scored goals into the void around him.

At thirty-six, the body negotiates. The pressing is gone, the tracking back is rationed, the ninety-minute engine that once defined him has been replaced by something more deliberate and more cold. He stands in the places where goals happen, and he waits, because he has spent twenty years learning exactly where those places are.

The VV tags carry the weight of the argument here. Goal Machine is self-evident, eighteen goals in a Premier League season from a striker who played for a team that finished sixth. Poacher captures the method, positional, ruthless, increasingly dependent on the penalty area rather than the pitch. But The Last Dance tag is the one that tells the real story, this was a season that felt like arrival and farewell simultaneously.
Eighteen goals. A broken club. An age that footballers are not supposed to reach and still matter. He mattered. Whether that was enough is a question Manchester United are still trying to answer.
notes.scout: This was not a renaissance. It was something narrower and more revealing: a finisher operating on instinct alone, stripped of the system, the teammates, the structure that amplifies great players, and still finding the net eighteen times in England's top division at an age when most forwards have already made peace with the past. You cannot deny the number. What you must weigh is what the number cost, and what it obscured.
notes.glance: Eighteen goals at thirty-six, for a club coming apart at the seams, from a man who has never once accepted the idea that time wins.

notes: Arsenal in 2020/21 were a team searching for a shape they had not yet found, and Saka was their most consistent act of faith. He played as a nominal central midfielder but lived everywhere, the kind of player a manager leans on precisely because the role does not contain him.

He was 19. Not 19 and thriving in a title-winning side with senior players absorbing the pressure around him. Nineteen, and the pressure was his. That distinction matters enormously when you try to place this season in its proper context.

Five goals and three assists from central midfield in the Premier League, at this age, without a settled team identity around him, carry a weight the raw numbers resist. No tags adorn this card, and that absence is its own kind of evidence, a season that predates the vocabulary the game would eventually find for him.
This was not the season Saka arrived. This was the season he refused to wait for permission.
notes.scout: At 19, in a Premier League side losing its way, Bukayo Saka was asked to be the answer before he had fully understood the question. Five goals and three assists do not tell the whole story, they tell the survivable part of it. What the numbers cannot hold is the weight of being the most trusted player at a club in transition, the one Arteta turned to when the plan needed rescuing, and that burden, worn this lightly at this age, is the proof of something rare.
notes.glance: A teenager carrying Arsenal's ideas on his back, and somehow, he did not buckle.

notes: Liverpool in 2020/21 were a club in genuine distress. Champions the year before, they became a side that lost seven consecutive home league games, that shipped goals from positions they had made sacred. The structure Jurgen Klopp had built with such precision was exposed, and exposed badly. Into that wreckage, Salah arrived every week.

He was 28, the age when a forward either finds a deeper gear or begins the long negotiation with decline. Salah found the gear. The Iron Man tag tells you he was present, game after game, when others were absent. The Clinical tag tells you presence was not enough, that he converted when lesser players in lesser form would have dragged the ball wide. This was not volume shooting. This was precision under pressure.

The Goal Machine tag is the one that requires the most honesty in this context. Goal machines need supply. They need runners beside them, width behind them, a midfield that can hold the ball and find the pockets. Liverpool provided almost none of that this season. The 5 assists confirm a man who still sought to connect, who did not retreat into selfishness when the team needed rescuing. A rating of 90 for a striker whose club finished third reflects exactly that, the output was personal, and it was extraordinary.

Some seasons a player carries a number on his back. This season, Salah carried a club. The goals did not save Liverpool's title, nothing could have, but they kept the dignity of their campaign intact. That is what 22 goals in wreckage actually means.
notes.scout: At 28, this was Salah in the furnace. Liverpool lost Virgil van Dijk in October, then Joe Gomez, then Joel Matip, and the title defence collapsed into a fight for fourth. The team around him was diminished, the system that made him lethal was fractured, and yet the numbers did not move. Twenty-two goals in the Premier League is what a functioning striker at a functioning club produces. Salah produced it while carrying the attack alone. You cannot look at this season and see a man benefiting from circumstances. You see a man refusing to be defined by them.
notes.glance: Twenty-two goals in the season Liverpool forgot how to win, and Salah never stopped scoring.

notes: This was a season defined by necessity as much as talent. Manchester United needed Bruno Fernandes to be everything at once, the creator, the finisher, the leader of last resort, and he answered every demand without flinching across thirty-seven league appearances.

There is something both heroic and quietly troubling about a 26-year-old becoming the gravitational centre of a club the size of United. The Iron Man tag is not a compliment in the traditional sense, it is a document of reliance, evidence that the machine around him required constant human intervention to keep moving.

The numbers are not supplementary here, they are the argument. Eighteen goals and twelve assists from a central attacking midfielder in the Premier League earns the Goal Machine, Clinical, Provider, Playmaker, and Maestro tags simultaneously, because each one describes a different facet of the same extraordinary output. No single tag captures him. All five are required just to approximate what he was.
Some players have great seasons. Bruno Fernandes had a necessary one, and the difference is that necessity leaves a mark that statistics alone cannot fully explain.
notes.scout: At 26, Bruno Fernandes was not merely productive, he was load-bearing. The kind of player whose absence reveals the structural cracks in everything around him, and whose presence papers over them so convincingly that the cracks go unexamined for another season. A VV rating of 90 from the CAM position in the Premier League is not a statistical achievement, it is a confession from the league itself that one man was operating at a frequency his environment could not match.
notes.glance: Eighteen goals, twelve assists, and a team carried on the shoulders of one Portuguese who refused to let Manchester United drift into irrelevance.

notes: In the Molineux engine room, Moutinho was the quiet current beneath a Wolves side searching for direction , the man who took the ball under pressure and made the next thing simple, which is the hardest thing in football to do consistently at any age, let alone this one.

The lunges become selections, the sprints become reads, the energy once spent covering ground is redirected into knowing where the ground will need covering next. Moutinho had been doing this since Braga, since Porto, since Monaco, since the European Championship that changed a country. By 20/21, he did not need to learn the game , he was the game.

The Engine Room tag is not decoration here , it is diagnostic. One goal and one assist in a CDM role across a Premier League season is not a creative indictment, it is structural honesty. A VV rating of 59 reflects a player operating within the defined limits of his role, protecting the backline, recycling possession, absorbing pressure so others could express. The numbers are sparse because the job demands sparseness.
The metronome does not need to be the loudest instrument in the orchestra , it simply needs to keep time when everything else threatens to lose it, and for one more season, Moutinho kept time.
notes.scout: This was not a season of revelation, it was a season of proof , that the metronome still ticks, that the passes still find angles younger men cannot see. One goal, one assist from a deep midfield role in the Premier League at thirty-four is not a number to apologise for , it is a testament to a career spent understanding that the game is not about scoring, it is about controlling. To deny this season its dignity is to misread what a defensive midfielder is actually for.
notes.glance: At thirty-four, in a league that devours the slow and discards the old, João Moutinho simply kept the engine running.

notes: West Brom in 2020/21 were not a Premier League side wearing Premier League shirts. They were outnumbered, outrun, outspent in almost every fixture they entered. Pereira played within that reality and somehow produced outside of it.

Eleven goals and six assists from a CAM in a relegated side is not a statistic, it is a testimony. Tagged Goal Machine, Clinical, and Playmaker, Pereira carried all three designations simultaneously, which is its own kind of rarity. The 93 rating tells you what the engine saw, a player whose output was elite for his role even before you factor in the structural weight of carrying an entire club's ambition on his own.

He did not save West Brom. But he left behind a season that asks a question no one has fully answered, what happens to Matheus Pereira when the players around him are good enough to receive what he gives.
notes.scout: Matheus Pereira produced numbers at West Brom in 2020/21 that would have decorated a mid-table team pushing for Europe, yet he produced them for a side that finished bottom, which is either the most damning context or the most illuminating one. At 24, this was his proof of concept delivered to the wrong address, a season that argues for what he could have been in a structure that deserved him, and the cruelty is that the argument never got a proper hearing.
notes.glance: A man playing like he belonged to a different league, because he did, and the Premier League never let him forget it.

Centre-back is a position that demands composure under pressure, the ability to see danger before it arrives. That he produced five assists from there tells you he was not just surviving the role, he was extending it.

One goal and five assists from centre-back in the Premier League. No tags have been awarded here, because the engine had no template for what this was. Sometimes the numbers exist outside the categories, not because the performance was insufficient, but because it was genuinely unexpected at this position and this age, in a league that offers no shelter to the young.

There are seasons that define a player and seasons that merely hint at what is coming. This was the hint, quiet and persistent, the kind you only fully understand years later when you look back and realise the evidence was always there.
notes.scout: This is the season that proved Saka was not a footballer of one shape but of pure footballing intelligence, the kind that adapts to whatever the team requires and still leaves a mark. A centre-back with five assists in the Premier League is not a statistic you file away, it is a character reference. You cannot watch this card and argue the ceiling, because the ceiling was never the point.
notes.glance: At eighteen, in a season the world stood still, Bukayo Saka played centre-back for Arsenal and still found five assists, as if the position were merely a suggestion and the contribution inevitable.

At twenty-three, in the Premier League, in a City side still recalibrating under Guardiola after the shock of losing the title, this season asked Rodri to anchor without yet being the anchor. He was steadying himself as much as the team.

Three goals and two assists from central midfield in a Premier League season are not decorative numbers for that position. They are evidence of intent, of a player who understood his attacking responsibility even while his primary work was structural, protective, the quiet geometry of midfield control.

Sixty-two. It feels low for what Rodri would become. But every great career has a chapter where the story is still being written, and this was that chapter, the one you return to later and think: it was always there, wasn't it. Always there.
notes.scout: This was not yet the finished article. Three goals, two assists, a VV rating of 62 from a central midfield role at the Etihad: the numbers are the numbers of a player finding his weight in a system that demands you carry it without ever being seen to strain. What the card does not show is the positioning, the refusal to panic, the early signs of a player who would come to define how City controlled matches from the inside out. You could already see what he was going to be. You just had to know where to look.
notes.glance: At twenty-three, Rodri was learning what Manchester City needed him to become, and the education was already visible in the stillness he brought to a midfield that had forgotten how to breathe.

An 81 rating across half a campaign is not a footnote, it is the opening sentence of something, and in the spring of 2020 at Old Trafford, opening sentences were all they had ever needed.

The Maestro tag is not given to players who fill a role, it is given to players who redefine one, and Fernandes did not inherit the number ten shirt so much as rescue it from years of quiet, accumulating grief. To deny this season its place in United's modern story is to misunderstand what desperation looks like when it is finally answered.

Compact, disciplined, built to frustrate, it was a structure that asked its central midfielder not to express himself but to control the tempo, to be the metronome in a machine designed for precision over spectacle. Moutinho was not diminished by those constraints. He defined them.

At thirty-three, most players in this position are managing themselves, protecting minutes, conserving energy. Moutinho was playing the full weight of a Premier League season, the Iron Man tag not a marketing flourish but a statement of physical fact. There is something almost defiant in it, the body refusing to negotiate with age on any terms but its own.

The Playmaker and Maestro tags are not interchangeable here. The Playmaker tag speaks to the six assists, the final pass found in traffic, the understanding of where the forward will be before the forward knows himself. The Maestro tag speaks to everything around the numbers, the positioning that eliminated danger before it arrived, the touch that bought three seconds where none existed. A VV rating of 79 from a central midfielder at this age, at this club, in this league, carries a weight the number alone cannot fully hold.

Some players leave a season behind them like a door closing. Moutinho left this one open, a reminder that football intelligence, when it reaches its fullest form, does not expire on any schedule the calendar recognises.
notes.scout: There is a version of this story where a Portuguese veteran at a newly-promoted Midlands club is a footnote, a warm body filling a squad role. Moutinho made that story impossible to tell. Six assists from central midfield in the Premier League at thirty-three is not a number that asks for context, it demands respect, because it proves that the read, the weight, the timing, the things that cannot be coached, were still operating at the highest level. You cannot deny this season without denying what technical mastery looks like when it outlasts the legs that used to carry it.
notes.glance: At thirty-three, in the most demanding league on earth, João Moutinho did not slow down, he simply made the game slow down around him.

notes: Trent Alexander-Arnold was 21 years old, playing for the best team in England, and somehow the most astonishing thing about him was not the trophy at the end. It was the Tuesday nights in January, the away legs in the rain, the crosses that found men who had not yet started their run.

Liverpool won the title by 18 points. Klopp's system asked full-backs to become wingers, midfielders, architects. Alexander-Arnold did not simply comply with that demand. Four goals and 13 assists. The Provider and Playmaker tags are not decorations here, they are a precise diagnosis. No right-back in Premier League history had delivered this volume of direct creation in a single season, and the Role Rarity dimension of the VV engine scores accordingly. The Wonderkid tag carries its own weight too: this was not a veteran finding one last peak. This was a 21-year-old at the beginning of something.
Some players win titles. Some players build them from the right flank, one outswinging corner at a time, until the whole architecture of a season reveals itself as their work.
notes.scout: At 21, Alexander-Arnold did not merely perform well in a championship-winning side. He redefined what the position is allowed to demand of the game. Thirteen assists from a defensive role in the Premier League is not a peripheral detail, it is the central argument: this was a player operating in a dimension his position had not previously occupied, and the 86 VV rating reflects exactly that structural rarity. You cannot dismiss this season. You can only decide whether you understood it while it was happening.
notes.glance: A right-back who finished the season with more assists than most number tens, and made the league title feel inevitable.

notes: There is a particular kind of season that changes the conversation around a player permanently. For Marcus Rashford at Manchester United in 2019/20, this was that season.

He carried the number on his back and the weight of a club still searching for itself in the years after Sir Alex Ferguson. At twenty-two, most players are still being managed carefully, their minutes rationed, their responsibility limited. Rashford accepted the full burden of expectation at Old Trafford and did not flinch from it.

Some seasons you file away as statistics. This one you file away as a turning point, the season Rashford stopped being Manchester United's most exciting young player and became, simply, their player.
notes.scout: A CAM producing at this level for Manchester United in the Premier League is not supplementary contribution, it is load-bearing architecture. The Iron Man tag tells you what the numbers alone cannot: Rashford was present, relentlessly, in a club that needed him to be, and the Marksman tag tells you the presence was purposeful. At twenty-two, this was not a glimpse of what he might become, it was the first full sentence of what he already was.
notes.glance: Seventeen goals and seven assists at twenty-two, Marcus Rashford did not emerge that season, he arrived.

notes: Arsenal in 2019/20 were a club negotiating an identity crisis in slow motion, and Lacazette wore that uncertainty in every game. He was asked to lead a line that could not consistently supply him, a Poacher without the service a poacher requires.

He turned 29 that summer and the season felt like a question left unanswered. Not a failure, precisely, but the kind of season that accumulates quietly in a career, the ones you remember not for what happened but for what was withheld.

The Marksman tag tells you his movement and finishing mechanics remained sound, and four assists show a man still committed to the collective when the individual moments dried up. But ten goals in the Premier League at 28 is the number that sits in the room and does not leave.

What stays is the image of a real footballer, technically honest, positionally intelligent, playing at the wrong moment in the wrong version of his club, and wondering, perhaps, what this career might have looked like somewhere else.
notes.scout: At 28, a striker should be arriving at the peak of his authority, the years of learning fused with the physical prime still present. Lacazette produced enough, tagged Marksman and Poacher, to remind you of the player Arsenal thought they had signed, but a VV rating of 87 and only ten league goals in a Premier League season is a career neither fulfilling its promise nor abandoning it entirely. The honest scout does not look away from that contradiction.
notes.glance: Ten goals and a quiet kind of suffering, Lacazette in 2019/20 was a craftsman working in a house that was falling down around him.

notes: Kevin De Bruyne at Manchester City in 2019 to 20 was the clearest expression yet of what Pep Guardiola had been building toward, a midfielder who could be simultaneously the brain and the fist of a football idea. City without a recognised striker for long stretches of that campaign, and De Bruyne simply absorbed the demand.

He was twenty-eight, the age when a footballer's ambition and execution finally occupy the same body at the same time. Twenty assists, a record for the division, is the Provider tag rendered in history. The Playmaker and Maestro dimensions on his radar are not decorations, they are the structural explanation for why those numbers exist at all, a man who made space for others and then, when no space was offered, scored himself.

The Premier League has seen creators and it has seen finishers, but it has rarely seen one man make the distinction feel irrelevant, and in 2019 to 20, Kevin De Bruyne made it feel irrelevant every single week.

The Iron Man tag tells you he was there for every movement of this symphony, the Maestro tag tells you he was leading it, and the Premier League's assist record, broken and claimed as his own, tells you that posterity was watching. To argue against this season is to argue against evidence.
